The page used to fetch 200 rows and show 15 per page, so yesterday's entries seemed to vanish behind today's sign-ins. It is now paged on the server across the full history, with filters: search, action, record type, by, date range and hide sign-ins. Records show readable names (e.g. 'Role · Regional HR', 'Employee · Subham Tripathy (TH5001)') instead of 'org_role #68'. A Details row shows the values. Every successful /admin write on v2 that the handler didn't audit itself is now logged generically as Created/Updated/Deleted/Published with the submitted values; passwords, PII and files are hidden. summary: Decision D4: the sign-in code (and the forgot-password code) goes to the employee's personal email until the official mailbox is confirmed, and always when the official address is a placeholder (example.com, *.example, *.test, *.invalid, *.local). The official mailbox counts as confirmed once a code sent to it has been used; accounts that signed in before this change are treated as confirmed. The code screen names the address ('your personal email s****9@gmail.com'). It offers 'Resend code' and 'Send it to my official/personal email instead'. On v2 the personal email can also be used as the sign-in ID (H44), when it belongs to exactly one active employee with a login.

negativeTests: 1. A wrong code. Expected: 'Invalid or expired code'. 2. A personal email shared by two employees, or belonging to a candidate. Expected: 'Invalid credentials'.

summary: On v2 the sign-in code is sent immediately inside the request. If the mail provider fails, the user sees "We couldn't send your sign-in code to …" (502) instead of 'code emailed', and the code is voided. The failure is recorded in email_queue and the audit log. The mailer now logs every send/failure, reports SendGrid's actual rejection reason, and warns when MAIL_FROM doesn't match the Gmail SMTP login (a common cause of silent drops). New Master-only diagnostics: GET /api/v2/admin/email-health and POST /api/v2/admin/email-health/test. Partial because production delivery itself (the personal-Gmail sender) can't be verified from here; ops should check it with the diagnostic.
testSteps: 1. As Master, call GET /app/api/v2/admin/email-health. Expected: provider, from address, warnings, 7-day counts and recent failures. 2. POST /api/v2/admin/email-health/test {"to":"you@gmail.com"}. Expected: ok, or the provider's exact error. 3. Log in as TKF9009. Expected: either the code arrives, or an on-screen error saying it couldn't be sent.
negativeTests: 1. With mail failing, sign in. Expected: "We couldn't send your sign-in code to …". 2. Company Super Admin calling email-health. Expected: 403.
automated: scripts/v2/test-auth.js — 'v2: send failure → 502 with a clear message', 'failed send recorded as FAILED', 'Master: provider description + queue health', 'Company Super Admin → 403'
v1Impact: v1 keeps queued delivery (no new errors); diagnostics are v2 only.
